breakfast.name: Ful Medames (Egyptian Fava Bean Stew)
breakfast.description: A hearty, nutritious Egyptian breakfast of slow-cooked fava beans with spices, topped with tahini, olive oil, and fresh vegetables. Ancient dish with roots in Egyptian history
ingredients: Fresh diced peppers, red onion, and tomato for topping
instructions: Soak dried fava beans overnight, then cook in water for 2-3 hours until very soft
Heat olive oil and sauté half the onion and cumin for 3 minutes
Add cooked beans and 100ml water, bring to boil and simmer for 1 minute
Mash beans with potato masher until partially crushed
Add remaining onion, tomatoes, lemon juice, salt and pepper
Simmer for 2 minutes until flavors meld
Top with tahini and olive oil
Garnish with diced peppers, red onion, and tomato
Serve with pita bread or fried eggs on the side
breakfast.notes: Can use canned fava beans to reduce cooking time. The partial mashing creates the proper creamy consistency with some whole beans remaining
breakfast.fun_fact: Ful Medames dates back to at least the fourth century in Egypt. The name means buried, referring to traditional slow-cooking method where beans were buried over gentle embers all night
alternatives: Serve with tahini sauce drizzled over
Add a fried egg on top

lunch.name: Falafel (Fried Chickpea Patties)
lunch.description: Egyptian fried chickpea patties served in pita bread with tahini sauce, lettuce and tomato. Popular lunch throughout Middle East
instructions: Drain soaked chickpeas
Pulse in food processor with onion, garlic, herbs until fine crumbles
Add spices, salt, pepper and flour
Form into small balls or patties
Heat oil to 350°F
Fry falafel 2-3 minutes per side until golden
Serve in pita with tahini sauce, lettuce and tomato
lunch.notes: Must use dried chickpeas, not canned. The moisture content affects texture significantly
lunch.fun_fact: Falafel became popular lunch in Egypt and throughout Middle East, served in pita with vegetables and tahini sauce

dinner.name: Koshari (Layered Rice, Lentils and Pasta with Sauce)
dinner.description: Egypt's national dinner dish - layered rice, lentils, pasta with tomato sauce
instructions: Cook lentils in salted water 20-25 minutes until tender but not mushy; drain
Cook rice in salted water until fluffy; fold in cooked lentils gently
Cook pasta al dente according to package directions; drain and toss with 1 tbsp olive oil
Toss sliced onions with flour and salt; deep fry at high heat until dark golden and crispy
Heat 2 tbsp oil, add minced garlic, cook until fragrant, add tomato puree and vinegar, simmer 10 minutes
Layer in bowls: rice and lentils mixture, topped with pasta
Pour sauce over and top with crispy fried onions
dinner.notes: The fried onions are crucial - they must be dark golden
dinner.fun_fact: Invented in 19th century Cairo as fusion of Indian, Italian and Egyptian cuisines
